title: Batching
hook: Jumping between emails, design, and calls all day feels busy. It's mostly just warming up over and over.
statement: Switching between tasks quietly kills your efficiency.
explainer: Every switch costs time to get your head back in. Group similar work into blocks and you spend more of the day doing, not restarting.
sop: List yesterday's tasks and tag each by type: creative, admin, communication.
Count how many times you switched types. That's your Switching number.
Group similar tasks for the week into one or two blocks.
Protect each block. No email, no messages, no other task types.
Track Output per block to confirm it's working.
equation_example: Output is 12 tasks done. Switching is 4 changes of task type. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 tasks per switch. Higher means you get more done before switching drains you. Lower means you're losing time re-orienting instead of working.
question: Pick one task you do in scattered bits and batch it into one weekly block.
closing_statement: Every switch costs more than the task itself.
caption:
Principle Nº 138: Batching

Jumping between emails, design, and calls all day feels busy. It's mostly just warming up over and over.

Switching between tasks quietly kills your efficiency.

Your turn: Pick one task you do in scattered bits and batch it into one weekly block.
